unlock.bannerText: Certificates cannot be issued or renewed until you unlock the CA keys.
unlock.title: Unlock the CA
unlock.description: Enter the CA passphrase (or HSM PIN) chosen during setup.

dashboard.description: Certificates, authorities and recent activity at a glance.
dashboard.nothingExpiringText: ACME clients renew automatically; manual certificates show up here before they expire.

ca.nameConstraintsHint: Optional. One permitted domain per line (e.g. home.lab); leave empty for no constraint.
ca.name: Name

authorities.description: Your root CA and the issuing CAs that sign certificates. Each issuer has its own ACME directory and policy.
authorities.createText: An issuing CA signed by the active root, with its own ACME directory, policy and EAB keys.
authorities.clonePolicyHint: Copy the policy of an existing issuer.
authorities.successorText: Generates a new root CA, cross-signed by the current one, so clients that trust the old root keep working. Use it well before the current root expires.
authorities.directoryText: Point your ACME clients to this URL.
authorities.setDefaultText: “{{name}}” will serve the default ACME directory and sign Conrad's own HTTPS certificate.
authorities.rotateText: Creates a new key and certificate for “{{slug}}”. The ACME URL stays the same; the old issuer is retired but its certificates remain valid.
authorities.revokeText: The issuer certificate is revoked by the root and its ACME directory stops working. Certificates it signed will no longer be trusted. This cannot be undone.

policy.title: Issuance policy
policy.description: What this issuer is allowed to sign, for ACME and manual requests.
policy.allowedDomainsHint: One per line. *.home.lab allows any name under home.lab; leave empty to allow anything.
policy.allowIPsHint: Allow IP SANs (validated with http-01 or tls-alpn-01).
policy.requireEABHint: Only ACME clients with an External Account Binding key can register.
policy.clientAuthHint: Add the clientAuth extended key usage (mTLS).
policy.accountsPerHour: New accounts per IP per hour

eab.title: External Account Binding
eab.description: Keys that let an ACME client register an account with this issuer.
eab.createText: Give the key a name so you know which client uses it.
eab.createdText: Copy the HMAC now: it is shown only once. Each key can bind a single ACME account.
eab.emptyText: Create one when you enable “Require EAB” or want to control which clients can register.
eab.revokeText: “{{name}}” can no longer be used to register new accounts.

certs.description: Every certificate signed by Conrad, from ACME clients and manual requests.
certs.issueText: Sign a certificate without an ACME client: let Conrad generate the key, or paste a CSR.
certs.issuedText: Download the certificate and the full chain.
certs.issuedKeyWarning: Download the private key now: Conrad does not keep it and cannot show it again.
certs.namesHint: DNS names or IP addresses, one per line.
certs.pfxPasswordHint: Optional: also create a PKCS#12 (.pfx) bundle.
certs.csrHint: Names and key are taken from the CSR.
certs.validityHint: Empty uses the issuer's default; capped by its policy.
certs.emptyText: Point an ACME client at an issuer or issue one manually.
certs.name: Name
certs.revokeText: Revoked certificates are listed in the CRL and reported by OCSP. This cannot be undone.

accounts.description: Accounts registered by ACME clients. Deactivating an account stops it from ordering certificates.
accounts.deactivateText: The client will no longer be able to order or renew certificates with this account. Its certificates stay valid.
accounts.emptyText: They appear when a client registers with an issuer's directory.

audit.description: Everything that happened in Conrad: sign-ins, issuance, revocations and configuration changes.

install.description: Devices only trust Conrad's certificates after the root CA is installed. Do it once per device.
install.verifyHint: The first download cannot be verified over HTTPS, because your device does not trust Conrad yet: compare the fingerprint above with the one printed by the commands.
install.next: Next: get certificates for your services.

fedora.s1: Download the root into the trust anchors:

arch.s1: Download the root and add it as a trust anchor:

ios.s1: Open the configuration profile in Safari and allow the download.
ios.s2: Go to Settings → General → VPN & Device Management, choose “Conrad” and install it.
ios.s3: Go to Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings and turn on full trust for the root.

android.s2: Go to Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate, and pick the file.
android.note: Many apps ignore user-installed CAs; browsers like Chrome accept them.

firefox.s1: Firefox has its own certificate store. On Windows and macOS it can reuse the system roots; on Linux point it at the file.
firefox.s2: Create policies.json in the Firefox distribution folder (e.g. /etc/firefox/policies/):

clients.eabRequired: This issuer requires an External Account Binding: replace <EAB_KID> and <EAB_HMAC> with a key.
clients.trustFirst: Clients must trust the root CA before they can talk to Conrad's ACME server.

notify.description: Get an email or a webhook call before certificates expire and when something goes wrong.
notify.usernameHint: Leave empty for relays without authentication.
notify.plaintextWarning: Credentials will be sent unencrypted. Use STARTTLS or TLS unless the relay is on a trusted network.
notify.skipVerify: Skip TLS certificate verification (self-signed mail servers)
notify.secretHint: Optional. Requests carry an X-Conrad-Signature HMAC-SHA256 header.
notify.emptyText: Add an email or webhook channel to be warned before certificates expire.
notify.thresholdsText: When to warn before a certificate expires. Renewed certificates are skipped.
notify.caThresholds: Root and issuer warnings are fixed at 90, 30, 7 and 1 days.

settings.description: Your account, sign-in methods and system information.
settings.accountText: The single administrator of this Conrad instance.
settings.languageText: Used for the interface and for emails.
settings.passwordText: Changing the password signs out every other session.
settings.oidcText: Sign in with Authentik, Authelia, Keycloak, Pocket ID or any OpenID Connect provider.
settings.redirectUrlHint: Register this URL in your identity provider.
settings.secretKept: Leave empty to keep the stored secret.
settings.allowedHint: Only this identity may sign in. Set at least one.
settings.passwordLoginText: Disable it once single sign-on works.
settings.passwordLoginWarning: If the identity provider is down you can re-enable password sign-in with the conrad CLI.
settings.backupText: A consistent snapshot of the database, including the encrypted CA keys.
settings.backupNote: Keys stay encrypted with your CA passphrase: keep the passphrase too, or the backup cannot be restored.

setup.passphraseHint: Encrypts the CA keys at rest. Needed after every restart unless set in the config.
setup.pinHint: PIN of the PKCS#11 token holding the keys.
